title: From Global to Tail Convergence: Dynamics of $\alpha$-Stable Score-Based Generative Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.19773v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Score-based generative models driven by $\alpha$-stable L{\'e}vy processes have been proposed as an alternative to Brownian diffusion models, with empirical evidence suggesting improved sampling and better modeling of heavy-tailed data. Yet theoretical guarantees for these models remain limited. We develop a non-asymptotic convergence analysis for scale-preserving $\alpha$-stable generative dynamics, covering both compactly supported and power-law targets. In p-Wasserstein distance, we quantify the effects of early stopping, initialization, score approximation, and time discretization, and show exponential decay of the initialization error. A comparison with Brownian dynamics reveals that global Wasserstein convergence alone does not fundamentally distinguish the two models: both initialization errors decay exponentially with the forward horizon on the common class of heavy-tailed targets. A sharp separation emerges instead in the tails.

translated_title: 从全局收敛到尾部收敛：α-稳定基于分数的生成模型的动力学
translated_abstract: 由α-稳定Lévy过程驱动的基于分数的生成模型已被提出作为布朗扩散模型的替代方案，经验证据表明其在采样方面有所改进，并能更好地建模重尾数据。然而，这些模型的理论保证仍然有限。我们对保持尺度的α-稳定生成动力学建立了非渐近收敛性分析，涵盖紧支撑目标和幂律目标。在p-Wasserstein距离下，我们量化了早停、初始化、分数逼近和时间离散化的影响，并证明初始化误差呈指数衰减。与布朗动力学的比较表明，仅凭全局Wasserstein收敛并不能从根本上区分这两种模型：在共同的重尾目标类别上，两种模型的初始化误差都随正向时间范围呈指数衰减。而一个鲜明的分离出现在尾部。
tldr: 本文对α-稳定基于分数的生成模型建立了非渐近收敛性分析，证明在全局Wasserstein距离下α-稳定动力学与布朗扩散模型表现相当，但两者在尾部收敛行为上存在本质区别。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes non-asymptotic convergence analysis for α-stable score-based generative models, showing that while α-stable and Brownian dynamics exhibit comparable global Wasserstein convergence, a sharp separation emerges in their tail convergence behavior.
